newsitem.title: FRANCE: GM may seek car ventures in Europe - Smith.
newsitem.headline: GM may seek car ventures in Europe - Smith.

text.p: General Motors Corp, which has signed an accord with Renault to develop light commercial vehicles, may strike joint ventures in Europe with Renault or other partners, Chairman John Smith said in a French newspaper interview.

Asked whether GM might expand on the accord signed with Renault in December, Smith told the Figaro newspaper, "At this stage, we haven't thought of that. Renault is a good partner and we're satisfied with the way our accords are coming along. Partnerships are multiplying in the auto industry. We could sign agreements for other joint ventures in Europe with Renault or others if it makes sense for both parties."

Smith said GM and its German-based Opel subsidiary did not suffer in Europe from overcapacity. "We don't have overcapacity in Europe or anywhere else. It's true that, temporarily, our capacities don't correspond totally with demand. We're trying to increase flexibility at our European plants."

Asked about Renault's plan to close its Vilvoorde plant in Belgium, Smith said he could understand the French company's overcapacity problem. "We don't have that problem today but we had to take painful measures in the early 1990s. Renault's management had to take action to reduce costs," he said.
